checks.finding: Terms, actors, states, inputs and outputs are concrete. Field Definitions fixes Resolver, Affected component, Matched Capability, capability_minimum_enforcement, Block and Resolver Evidence; REQ-001's CLI block fixes every flag and its default; REQ-002 closes the diagnostic enum at sixteen named rows; REQ-004 fixes Evidence cardinality bindings by declaration_index. I checked REQ-001 step (m)'s repaired predicate specifically (requirements.md:334-338): 'this invocation's own publication transaction leaves no publication artifact standing' is well-formed and selects correctly for a first resolve (nothing published) and a re-resolve (the explicit clause that bytes a PRIOR successful resolve published and this invocation never touched do not count), and for both step-(m) rollback ids. Two imprecisions in the surrounding universal claim do not meet the evidence gate because no behavior is left undecidable: (a) 'except the two REQ-002 names AC-012 excepts' excludes disabled-legacy-invocation, which plainly does satisfy the predicate, but its direct-write route is independently fixed by Main Workflows 4 (:1096-1097), REQ-004 (:626-633) and Security Boundaries (:1275-1279); (b) the claim's justification 'their own rollback is what leaves nothing standing' is false for REQ-002's own acknowledged sub-case (:417) where the in-process rollback cannot fully complete, but AC-012 still compels the Evidence write and no alternate route exists. Both are Minor clarifications, not downstream mismatches.

REQ-003's advisory/required byte-identity guarantee contradicts its own amendment parenthetical on the Full track, and AC-016/TEST-016 is unsatisfiable there. requirements.md:462-481 guarantees byte-identical output across the track-exclusive set, naming 'the three Full-track artifacts facet-manifest.yaml/project-context.resolved.json/Resolver Evidence', and permits exactly three differences, all inside Resolver Evidence: 'only Resolver Evidence's own state field and its two enforcement-derived context_binding digest fields -- full_context_revision and projection_sha256 -- differ'. AC-016 (requirements.md:897) and TEST-016 (acceptance-tests.md:65) restate that scope, naming {facet-manifest.yaml, project-context.resolved.json} as one applicable set. The same parenthetical supplies the disproof: those digests hash 'the canonical Project Context text and the canonical Context Projection text, which copies workflow verbatim'. Two artifacts inside the guaranteed set must therefore differ across an advisory/required pair, and neither is reached by the exception. (1) generated/project-context.resolved.json IS that canonical Context Projection (AC-003, requirements.md:884), whose schema fields are fixed at investigation.md:136-138 as schema, source_sha256, workflow, components, shared_paths[] -- it carries workflow, hence workflow.capability_enforcement, verbatim, plus source_sha256, the hash of the differing canonical Project Context; its whole bytes differ, and the exception names only fields of Resolver Evidence. (2) facet-manifest.yaml carries context_binding {full_context_revision, dependency_pointers[], projection_sha256, registry_digest, ownership_digest} (investigation.md:128-131, INV-004), so it carries the identical two digests REQ-003 itself calls 'internally impossible' to hold identical, while the carve-out is scoped to 'Resolver Evidence's own' copies. Downstream failure mode: the Phase-2 test author cannot construct TEST-016's Full-track fixture pair, and any passing implementation must silently widen the permitted-difference set, which is spec content nobody has reviewed. Spec-stage, because both halves of the conflict are in requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md, not in design or implementation. Critical per the calibration's 'impossible acceptance criteria' class. Origin, for the remediator only: the B(1) amendment (investigation.md:854-862, human-approved 2026-08-24) recognised the impossibility and propagated the carve-out to the Resolver Evidence instance alone; the Lite track is genuinely unaffected because capability-summary.schema.json has no context_binding (investigation.md:132-135), which is why the existing enforcement-byte-identity driver (investigation.md:879-887) can pass while the Full-track half cannot.

Negative, empty, boundary and failure paths implied by the requirements are covered by named, independently-triggerable fixtures. TEST-010 gives one fixture per each of the sixteen Block ids plus a clean negative; TEST-011/TEST-038 cover no-partial-artifact including post-staging Blocks; TEST-018 covers the zero-affected-component empty state and its []-cardinality subtlety; TEST-027 covers all three any-branch WARN cases after B2 removed the accepted-WARN branch; TEST-047 covers both the convergeable crash and the unconvergeable-journal Block, with both halves of the live-state obligation required of the one fixture; TEST-048/TEST-049 cover the pre- and post-publication TOCTOU windows including the affected_components-set-difference-alone case; TEST-055 splits output-schema-validation-failed into its two sub-cases; TEST-056 covers the abort-with-forwarded-warns shape; TEST-057/TEST-058 isolate the two ruling-C sub-triggers; TEST-050/051/054 cover validator provenance binding and the reader-side torn-state case; TEST-045 covers the four-way metamorphic matrix and order invariance; TEST-013 covers all three exit codes. The one thin spot -- the sub-case at requirements.md:417 where the in-process rollback cannot itself complete -- is explicitly named with a stated recovery owner (the next invocation's crash-recovery scan), is materially exercised by TEST-047's equivalent post-crash journal state, and has its detail-recording obligation locked by AC-039/TEST-039. The Lite required-present-empty state's absence of a fixture is documented at acceptance-tests.md:58 with a substantive reason (no schema-conformant Registry can express the key today), which is a disclosed limit rather than a coverage gap.

All three Assumptions (requirements.md:1337-1362) are resolved against investigation evidence or carry an explicit, owned re-verification step: the four sibling contracts' Passed status is confirmed per-worktree at INV-002 with a stated follow-up-edit obligation if any changes materially; the protected-suffix reservation's possible non-liveness is assigned to the future implementation task with a named alternative sequencing (INV-003); the SKILL.md unprotected status is declared a live snapshot to be re-verified at task start (INV-017). Open Questions are equally disposed: OQ-003 is resolved by INV-020 to a file:line anchor with a position-sensitive fingerprint guard (AC-053/TEST-053), and OQ-001/OQ-002 are explicitly deferred to a named future caller and matched by a Non-goal and a soft-dependency entry rather than left dangling. The one live cross-epic gap -- INV-019's missing required_lite_checks source -- is not an unresolved assumption but a named prerequisite with an owner (Epic A2's maintainers), a scope, a migration note, a fail-closed consequence (REQ-002), and a Risk entry, and the package explicitly declines to invent a source.

Every governance and irreversible-change boundary in scope is stated and testable. Authority boundaries: this package may not edit any A1/A2/A3/A4 contract or add the required_lite_checks field (Non-goals, requirements.md:810-821), and may not touch plugins/** -- locked by AC-032/TEST-032 as a git diff assertion over this package's own two commits. Write-authority boundaries: Roles and Permissions (:1003-1032) separates the human-copy route for immutable script code from the running-Resolver route for generated artifacts, correcting the M7 error of treating project-context.resolved.json as a human-copy target, and declares all four output artifacts agent-writable-only-via-the-Resolver. Fail-closed boundaries: disabled-legacy is a refusal, not a degraded mode, with no code path producing a Facet Manifest while the pipeline is derived-inactive (Security Boundaries :1259-1267), locked by AC-015/TEST-015 and independently by AC-042/TEST-042's caller spy harness; the never-silently-degrade caller rule is locked by AC-031/TEST-031 with a direct citation. Irreversible-change boundaries: publication is a journaled multi-target transaction whose rollback, recovery and no-partial-artifact obligations are locked by AC-011/TEST-011, AC-039/TEST-039, AC-047/TEST-047 and AC-049/TEST-049, each of which requires both halves of its obligation of a single fixture so neither can be satisfied vacuously. The unconvergeable-journal case correctly reserves manual operator intervention and forbids automatic repair. Amendment authority itself is recorded with verbatim dated human quotations at investigation.md:836-862.

Apart from the separately reported CONTRADICTION, the package hands off without requiring the design or implementation-policy reviewer to invent product behavior. The CLI surface, flag defaults and usage-error class are fixed; the processing order is fixed as a lettered step sequence (0)-(m) with the staged-generation invariant stated structurally rather than as a per-step promise; the Block taxonomy is a closed sixteen-row table with per-row trigger conditions and an explicit no-fail-open claim; the new contract's every field, cardinality binding, keying rule and bidirectional-consistency rule is fixed in REQ-004, as is the companion validator's own closed twelve-value enum; the caller integration contract names a concrete file:line insertion point with a fingerprint guard rather than a prose position. Every REQ maps to at least one AC and every AC except the three documented Global rows maps 1:1 to a TEST row, with the exception class itself justified against two sibling packages' precedent. The reported contradiction does not itself change this judgement, because its remedy is a scope repair whose correct answer is already derivable from the package's own INV-004 schema field lists (the projection carries workflow; the Manifest's context_binding carries the two digests; the Summary carries neither) rather than product behavior that must be newly decided.
